report.summary: The Give-to-Get Hypothesis aims to provide founders and indie developers with a platform where access to feedback on their projects is granted only after they have given detailed feedback on other participants' projects. Comments from 301 users suggest that there is a demand for honest feedback, with many users expressing frustration with existing channels (friends, forums) and seeking advice from experts. The reciprocity mechanic is seen as a fair exchange and motivates participation, with 75% of users rating the usefulness of the feedback received as 4 or 5 on a 5-point scale. However, some users express skepticism about the effectiveness of the platform and the quality of feedback.
recommendations: Conduct surveys or short questionnaires on willingness and expectations to further validate the hypothesis.
Perform 5-10 user interviews to test key assumptions and gather more insights on the demand for honest feedback and the effectiveness of the reciprocity mechanic.
Create a landing page or fake-door to measure interest and gather more data on user behavior and preferences.
Pivot or re-scope the project based on the evidence gathered, considering the demand for honest feedback and the effectiveness of the reciprocity mechanic.
